A complete-item claim is assessed under its event mapping even when the same workshop owns other insured equipment. The highest dollar limit in this document is not a selectable alternative. There is no stacking of benefit limits, no replacement of a part sublimit by a full-item limit, and no deduction of another benefit's deductible. A beneficiary may not reclassify a component as a whole item to obtain a larger ceiling. All facts needed to identify the single claimed item are in the incident file.

BENEFIT B3: speaker damage
This benefit applies only to the named event speaker damage. A claim for a complete speaker and a claim for its tweeter both use this benefit. Its limit is $800.00; deductible $75.00; the part sublimit is $300.00 and applies only when the claimed item is the tweeter. The complete item has no part sublimit. Waiting period: 0 elapsed calendar days after inception; a loss on the boundary day is eligible. Usage above 800 hours excludes the loss; exactly that usage is allowed. Usage is measured at incident time.
The tweeter sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.

Usage is measured at incident time.
The glass top sublimit cannot be borrowed by a claim under another benefit. Related accessory mentions do not change which item was damaged. Cosmetic damage with no functional loss and ordinary wear are excluded. A technician-confirmed sudden functional failure or accidental impact of the named kind can qualify, subject to all other conditions. Repair and replacement are alternative bases, not cumulative payments; the stated eligible loss already uses the approved basis. Do not add accessory costs that are not part of that loss.
